text:
Connor Bedard has 12 points in 11 games and the Blackhawks have lost eight of his last ten. That gap is the story of Chicago's autumn. "WE all said we think we're going to win this year," he said, as quoted by The Athletic's Mark Lazerus. Now head coach Jeff Blashill is under pressure, and Bedard has publicly backed him.

His own game is in a good place. He is getting 1.32 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, well up on last season, and his 3.19 points per 60 sits inside our likely range rather than above it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs the eye test: he carries the puck in on 63% of his entries and gets to the dangerous ice at a 91st-percentile rate. He's shooting 11.4%, a touch below normal, so the goals could tick up.

The problem is the other end. Chicago gets only 41.9% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents gaining more against him than against almost any forward last season. Twenty-one-year-old stars usually learn that part late. Chicago needs him to learn it faster.
headline: Bedard is producing while Chicago sinks
